title: Introduce init-batch-controller, composable-hook-templates and encrypted-values-schema for private installs
author: Priya Rao
description: Motivation: Private installs can stall or overload control-plane when many tenants bootstrap at once and operators need safer secrets handling for on-prem deployments. This PR adds an init-batch-controller to gate and schedule tenant init jobs, introduces composable hook template primitives so chart maintainers can author smaller hook fragments and compose them per-tenant, and adds an encrypted-values schema to make opt-in secret encryption first-class in the Helm layer. Scope: chart changes live under charts/private and top-level templates; runtime controller is a lightweight Kubernetes controller (deployment manifest included) that batches Job launches based on namespace labels and a concurrency window. The values schema is additive and backwards compatible: default encryption is off to avoid surprise. The hook compositor is implemented as Helm template helpers (templates/_hook_compositor.tpl) and exposes templating primitives used by existing init jobs, allowing per-tenant override of phases. This also wires a safe-rollback annotation that prevents automated rollbacks from deleting init-state keys for tenanted installs. Testing: unit tests for helm template rendering, controller integration tests in the perf-canary suite, and an upgrade path test (helm upgrade --install with preserved values). Migration: operators should enable encryptedValues: true and provide an encryption key via values.encryption.kmsKeyRef or use the included encrypt-values.sh helper to generate a sealed payload for the encryptedValues.encrypted field. Rollout plan: merged to main, will be staged to release/v1.45 with a canary enabling the controller in 2 non-prod clusters before full rollout.

review_thread: Daniel Kim (reviewer) 2026-02-27: Please document the failure modes if the batch-controller crashes mid-wave; ensure jobs are idempotent. Also add metrics for queue depth.

Priya Rao (author) 2026-02-28: Added readiness/liveness and a leader-election flag; controller persists batch state in a ConfigMap and guarantees at-least-once start semantics. Added prometheus metrics: init_batch_wave_total and init_batch_queue_size.

merge_commit_summary: Squash merge: introduce init-batch-controller, hook compositor and encrypted values schema; add helper script and docs
release_notes: Add optional init-batch-controller to rate bootstrapping of tenant init jobs; add hook compositor templates for modular init hooks; add encryptedValues opt-in schema and helper for on-prem secret encryption. Backwards compatible: encryption off by default.
notes_for_ops: If enabling encryptedValues, provide encryption.kmsKeyRef or pre-seal values with scripts/encrypt-values.sh and set values.encryption.encrypted. Monitor init_batch_queue_size and init_batch_wave_total; default concurrency is 10 jobs per wave. For upgrade, run helm diff or template to verify per-tenant hook fragments have not been removed.
testing_instructions: 1) helm template charts/private -f examples/tenant-values.yaml | grep -A3 hook-compose to validate composition. 2) Apply controller manifest in a staging cluster and create 50 tenant namespaces with label init=batch-test to observe batching. 3) Toggle values.encryption to true and validate decryption path with provided kmsKeyRef or decrypt helper.
customer_impact: Low by default. Installs that opt-in to encryptedValues or enable the controller will change bootstrap timing (batched) and must account for potential wave delays. Operators should not enable controller and encryption at the same time during a live upgrade without testing in staging.
